reply.text: The selected lead target is the program effect on the treated population, aggregated as a horizon profile for horizons 0, 1, and 2, within the admitted window of support [lead.selection.requested.aggregation, lead.selection.requested.population, lead.selection.requested.horizons.0, lead.selection.requested.horizons.1, lead.selection.requested.horizons.2, lead.selection.requested.support]. The admitted averaging policy is "treated_cell_shares", which means the summary gives each treated unit-period equal weight within its requested cohort or horizon [lead.selection.requested.weighting, rel:context.claim:target.weighting]. Designs with different weights or support cannot be treated as equivalent, even if their estimates appear similar, because they are measuring different target populations, temporal supports, or weights [comparisons.0.reason, comparisons.5.reason]. Assumptions are statements about the underlying causal model that are proposed or taken as true, such as the parallel trends assumption [rel:parallel_trends.account], the spillover assumption [rel:spillover.account], the selection assumption [rel:selection.third party], and the anticipation assumption [rel:anticipation.units]. Diagnostics, like the pre-trends check [check:d906d39db4836.all.pre_trends], are data-driven tests that provide evidence but do not prove the underlying assumptions. For example, passing the pre-trends diagnostic does not prove parallel trends [check:d906d39db4836.all.pre_trends.detail].
